test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 8 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Consider the below statement and identify the correct answer.

Statement I: The reaction between an acid and a base to form salt and water is known as a neutralisation reaction.

Statement II: A neutralisation reaction can be written as: Acid + Base → Salt + Water

options.text: Statement I is correct, and Statement II is incorrect
Statement II is correct, and Statement I is incorrect.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Both statements are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The neutralization reaction is the reaction between an acid and a base where both neutralise the effect of each other.
 
• In this reaction, heat is always produced, or evolved.
 
• In the neutralisation reaction, a new substance is formed is called salt.
 
• *Acid+Base → Salt+Water (Heat is evolved)*
 
• For example - Hydrochloric acid (HCl) + Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) →Sodium chloride (NaCl) + Water (H2O).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
